terms.gloss: an ornament for the hair, a head-dress
evidence: Lucr. 1.88 (Lewis & Short): an ornament for the hair or head, a head-dress
terms.comment: A rare word, and in Lewis & Short an ornament for the hair rather than the style itself; Traupman uses it for a hairdo. To do someone’s hair is the verb cōmere; the cut or style of the hair is tōnsus.

terms.gloss: the cut or style of the hair
evidence: Plaut. Am. 1.1.288: pēs, statūra, tōnsus, oculī (Lewis & Short: “the cut or mode of dressing the hair”)

sources: Lewis & Short: como
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 160, 161, 164, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
